name: Euclidean remainder greatest common divisor
definition: For nonnegative integers a,b not both zero, gcd(a,b)=gcd(b,a mod b) when b>0; gcd(a,0)=a.
variables: a,b nonnegative integers; mod integer remainder; gcd greatest common divisor
assumptions: Exact integer arithmetic; at least one nonzero operand
limitations: For M=max(a,b)≥1, O(log(M+1)) remainder operations and a constant number of integer registers; bit cost depends on operand length and division implementation. Not a constant-time or factorization algorithm
failure_conditions: Both inputs zero or noninteger input.
computation: While b>0 simultaneously replace (a,b) by (b,a mod b). Return a when b=0. If a<b the first step swaps operands. Use exact integer remainder.

source.citation: K.-D. Crisman, Number Theory: In Context and Interactive, section 2.3, Algorithm 2.3.3 and proof reviewed, https://math.gordon.edu/ntic/ntic2019/section-euclid-alg.html ; remainder-operation bound independently derived.

required_inputs: Two nonnegative integers, not both zero.
mechanism_note: Distinct arithmetic algorithm. Writing a=qb+r proves that the common divisor sets of (a,b) and (b,r) agree. Remainders decrease until zero. If r>b/2 then b mod r=b−r<b/2; otherwise r≤b/2 already. Every two steps at least halve a positive divisor. Pick's lattice-area record uses gcd as a primitive, not this computation.

name: Sieve of Eratosthenes prime enumeration
definition: For integer N≥2, mark 2,…,N initially; for each still marked p with p²≤N, clear p²,p²+p,…≤N; the marked set P={q∈[2,N]:q is prime}.
variables: N inclusive bound; p candidate divisor; P returned prime set
limitations: O(N log log N) indexed word operations asymptotically using the standard prime reciprocal sum bound; O(N) flags plus output storage. Cost is exponential in the bit length of N; no claim of optimality or suitability for isolated large primality queries
failure_conditions: Invalid bound, insufficient memory or overflow in p².
computation: Initialize flags 2 through N true and 0,1 false. Scan p upward while p≤floor(N/p), clearing p² through N in increments of p only if p remains marked. Enumerate survivors in order; use checked indices and increments.

source.citation: M. Beckman, University of Illinois CS 491 CAP, 2019, The Sieve of Eratosthenes transcript, square-root reasoning, square-start marking and asymptotic bound reviewed, https://courses.physics.illinois.edu/cs491cap/fa2019/transcripts/sieve-of-eratosthenes/ ; finite inclusive-bound specification independently derived.

mechanism_note: Distinct prime enumeration algorithm. Each cleared value is composite. Every composite c has least prime divisor p≤sqrt(c), so c≥p² and is cleared at p; p itself cannot be cleared by smaller primes. Work is bounded by N plus N times the sum of reciprocals of primes up to sqrt(N); the standard Mertens prime-reciprocal bound gives O(N log log N). This is not independent trial division of each candidate.
